assumptions: Resident individual rates for 2026–27: 15% from $18,201, 30% from $45,001, 37% from $135,001, 45% from $190,001 (legislated stage of the 2025 tax cuts).
Medicare levy of 2%. Singles pay none up to $28,011 of taxable income and a reduced levy up to $35,013. These are the 2025–26 thresholds, carried forward until the 2026–27 indexation is announced.
Medicare levy surcharge tiers (singles, no dependants) for 2026–27: 1% from $105,001, 1.25% from $123,001, 1.5% from $164,001, on income for surcharge purposes.

Study loan (HELP/VSL/SSL) compulsory repayments use the marginal system that started in 2025–26: 15% of repayment income between $69,528 and $129,717, then 17% above, until the repayment reaches 10% of all repayment income at $186,051; from there it is 10% of the total.
Low income tax offset of up to $700, phasing out from $37,500.

Super Guarantee reference rate of 12% (from 1 July 2025). Personal deductible contributions stop at the concessional cap: anything above it earns no deduction, so the estimate never contributes past it.
GST of 10% (1/11 of a GST-inclusive price). Registration is generally required once GST turnover reaches $75,000.

Company tax at the base rate entity rate of 25% (aggregated turnover under $50 million and no more than 80% passive income), otherwise 30%. Dividends are franked at the company's rate and the franking credit is refundable.
ASIC annual review fee for a proprietary company of $342 for 2026–27; ASIC indexes it each 1 July.
Concessional contributions cap of $32,500 from 1 July 2026 (up from $30,000). Company-paid director super is capped at it; the quarterly maximum contribution base is not modelled.

Division 293: once taxable income plus concessional super contributions passes $250,000, those contributions attract an extra 15% on the lesser of the contributions and the amount over $250,000. It is included in the tax estimate.

A contract that makes a loss is shown as tax of zero, not as a refund against your other income: the non-commercial loss rules often stop that loss being claimed this year. A company that makes a loss is shown as paying no company tax; from 2026–27 it may be able to carry the loss back against company tax paid in the previous two years (limited by its franking account), which the estimate does not include.

Standard deduction for work-related expenses of up to $1,000 from 2026–27, without receipts, for anyone earning salary, wages or director fees; claiming more replaces it rather than adding to it. It applies to a job, a casual role, a labour-hire contract and a company director's salary, not to business income or income attributed under the personal services income rules.
Casual loading of 25%, as in most modern awards; a particular award or agreement may differ.
Annual leave loading of 17.5%, as in most awards and agreements. Many salaried professional roles pay no loading, so it is off by default.
Permanent employment follows the National Employment Standards: a 38-hour week, 4 weeks of annual leave and 10 days of paid personal leave.

Calendar dates: quarterly BAS due 28 October, 28 February, 28 April and 28 July; the income tax return due 31 October, or 15 May the following year through a registered tax agent. A due date on a weekend or national public holiday moves to the next business day. Super guarantee for quarters up to June 2026 is due on the 28th of the month after the quarter (the last is 28 July 2026); from 1 July 2026 Payday Super applies and an employer's super has to reach the fund within 7 business days of each payday. A personal deductible contribution has to reach the fund by 30 June to count for the year.
